recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future publisher regression causes the Encounter.serviceType terminology binding to disappear from rendered definitions or generated StructureDefinition output.
issue_request: FHIR-14477 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration change request from STU3 asking that Encounter.serviceType have a binding to a value set. The resolution recorded that the element was already bound to the example Service Type value set and that a build issue had prevented the binding from displaying accurately.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-14477 was found. Historical source inspection showed the pre-2021 Encounter spreadsheet already contained EncounterServiceType and http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/service-type, and the 2021 source refactor commits carried that binding into source/encounter/structuredefinition-Encounter.xml.
additional_context: Encounter and HealthcareService are active resources in source/fhir.ini, and the Service Type ValueSet is defined in active source/healthcareservice/valueset-service-type.xml. The current CI build renders Encounter.serviceType with Terminology Binding Service Type using an example binding, so the historical display problem is no longer present in the current build.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source files were changed because the authoritative current Encounter StructureDefinition already binds Encounter.serviceType to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/service-type with example strength, matching the Jira resolution.
